title: Assessment onboarding and auditstream playbook
content:
Purpose
This playbook is an operational checklist and coordination guide for onboarding external assessments (third-party penetration tests and purple/red-team exercises) that exercise RBAC v2, audit log schema, evidence automation, and SIEM exports. It is intentionally pragmatic: mix of checklist items, ownership, example log mappings, and quick remediation templates. Use this as the single source-of-truth during the assessment window.

Scope
- Environments: staging (primary for active testing), preprod (secondary), and production-only if explicitly requested and approved.
- Components in-scope: auth/identity service (RBAC v2), API gateway, serving runtime (model endpoints), audit-log pipeline (collector -> kafka -> enrichment -> s3/elastic), SIEM exports (Splunk/Datadog/Elastic integration), evidence automation artifacts (signed snapshots, retention manifests).
- Out-of-scope by default: vendor-managed infra (managed db instances), customer tenant data (unless explicit consent).

High-level timeline (recommended)
- Week -3: Intake form + risk approval + scopes signed.
- Week -2: Test plan shared, temporary test accounts created, RBAC sandbox role matrix provided.
- Week -1: Evidence pipeline health check + SIEM export smoke tests.
- Test week: Live coordination channel, daily 30-min sync, runbook on-call.
- Post-test +3 days: Consolidated findings draft. +10 days: remediation plan agreed.

Pre-engagement checklist (owner tags in parentheses)
- Intake form completed: scopes, IP allow list, testing windows (sec-team).
- Signed NDA + ATO adjustments (legal/security).
- Test principals and contact list (sec-ops).
- Create time-limited test identities: role_asm_test, role_audit_reader_test, role_service_account_test (iam). Note: assign minimal permissions then escalate if requested; document changes.
- Publish RBAC v2 role matrix snapshot (product-auth).
- Snapshot of audit log schema and sample records (observability).
- Ensure evidence bucket write permissions and lifecycle policy are set to prevent accidental deletion (infra).
- Prepare SIEM ingest keys and temporary index for assessment data (sre/observability).
- Run synthetic traffic and confirm baseline logs for the test window (sre).

Evidence automation and collection
- Stream collection points: API gateway logs, auth service events, serving-runtime request traces, audit enrichment service, DB DML change events (if applicable).
- Canonical evidence artifact types: raw log bundles (gzipped daily), signing manifest (sha256 list), alert captures (SIEM alerts), video captures of console actions (when applicable), packet captures only when explicitly allowed.
- Naming convention: assessment-<vendor>-<env>-<YYYYMMDD>-<artifact-type>. Example: assessment-redteam-staging-20260214-auditlogs.gz
- Automation notes: use the assessment-run lambda (git PR ref in linked_artifacts) to create time-limited exports. Default retention for assessment artifacts: 90 days unless legal requests longer.

Audit log schema (quick reference)
- core fields to require in every record: timestamp, event_id, actor_id, actor_role, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome (success/failure), request_id, source_ip, user_agent, trace_id.
- enrichment fields: model_id, seq_len, latency_ms, batch_id, kv_cache_hit (true/false), quantization_profile (if applicable).
- Suggested SIEM field mapping:
  - siem.timestamp <- timestamp
  - siem.event_id <- event_id
  - user.id <- actor_id
  - user.roles <- actor_role (csv)
  - http.method <- action (generate mapping for non-http actions)
  - resource.type <- resource_type
  - resource.id <- resource_id
  - outcome <- outcome
  - network.src.ip <- source_ip
  - trace.id <- trace_id
  - meta.model_id <- model_id
- Minimum retention on raw logs for investigations: 180 days in compressed cold storage.

SIEM export plan and smoke tests
- Targets in use: Splunk (enterprise customers), Datadog (platform telemetry), Elastic (internal). Each exporter must:
  - Support bulk batched export every 10s or streaming per event (configurable).
  - Gracefully backpressure to s3 when downstream is unavailable.
- Smoke test steps:
  1) Create a synthetic event with known event_id X and actor role 'test-role'.
  2) Push event through collector.
  3) Confirm delivery in target SIEM within 60s.
  4) Run SIEM query: event_id:X and actor_role:test-role -> must return the sample.
  5) Validate field mappings (timestamp parity, trace_id present).
- Alerting: if delivery latency > 2 min for >3 consecutive minutes trigger incident channel #siem-exports.

RBAC v2 focus areas for assessors
- Role enumeration: ensure test roles exist and document what permissions are intentionally omitted.
- Privilege escalation paths: capture all role-change events and service-account impersonation calls.
- Admin API surfaces: ensure rate-limiting, MFA gates, and audit logging are turned on.

Findings intake and triage process
- Findings format requested from assessor: title, description, reproducible steps, PoC artifacts, severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low), affected environments, suggested mitigation, references.
- Triage cadence: security triage daily during test week. Assign a ticket in Jira (prefix SEC-TEST) within 8 hours of receiving a valid finding.
- Severity mapping guidelines:
  - Critical: data exfiltration in production or full-value account compromise.
  - High: privilege escalation or bypassing RBAC on sensitive resources.
  - Medium: ability to trigger resource-intensive queries without immediate billing controls.
  - Low: informational or UX issues.

Remediation plan template (to paste into Jira ticket)
- Title: <original finding title> - REDWOOD REMEDIATION DRAFT
- Owner: <team> @<engineer>
- Description: short summary of issue + link to evidence bundle
- Root cause: brief investigation notes
- Short term mitigation (1–7 days): steps to reduce impact (e.g., revoke test account, block IPs, adjust policies)
- Long term fix (30–90 days): code/config changes, tests to add (e.g., auth integration tests, audit log assertions), rollout plan (canary -> full), verification steps (retest by assessor or automated tests)
- Post-fix monitoring: SIEM rule to detect recurrence for 90 days

Communication runbook
- Channel: #sec-assessments (create private thread for vendor).
- Emergency escalation: page on-call SRE + security lead for Critical findings.
- Daily status: short bullets, created tickets, open items, blockers.
- Post-test exec summary: 1 page with high-level impact, top 3 findings, and remediation timeline (to be drafted by security lead).

Common pitfalls and gotchas (from past exercises)
- Missing trace_id in some legacy audit events — add a lightweight wrapper that injects trace id before collector.
- SIEM field mismatch: vendor fields sometimes come in snake_case vs camelCase; normalize early in enrichment.
- Evidence manifests without hashes — make signing mandatory for official evidence.
- RBAC matrix snapshot drift: lock the snapshot commit id in git and reference it in intake form.

Open questions and action items (quick list)
- Q: Do we allow packet captures for external testers? A: Only on staging and with explicit approval from legal; update intake form to require this checkbox. (action: Priya)
- Q: Should retention default be 180 days for all assessment artifacts? A: Recommend 90 days for most, 180 for critical findings; formalize in policy. (action: Marco)
- Action: Emily to add SIEM exporter smoke test to the CI pipeline (ticket: SEC-OBS-77).
- Action: Jonas to publish RBAC v2 snapshot script and sample role list to Confluence.

Appendix: quick CLI snippets
- Export logs for a 2-hour window to s3 (example):
  aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /redwood/audit --start-time 1700000000000 --end-time 1700007200000 --output json | gzip > assessment-<vendor>-<date>-auditlogs.gz
- Generate manifest (sha256) for bundle:
  sha256sum assessment-*-auditlogs.gz > manifest-sha256.txt

Notes to reviewers
- This document is intentionally operational and pragmatic. Feedback requested: missing checklist items, permission granularity suggestions, or local SIEM mappings we should add.

Revision history
- 2025-11-02: Initial draft (Aisha)
- 2025-12-18: Added SIEM smoke test steps and evidence naming conventions (Emily)
- 2026-02-28: Updated retention and open actions after recent assessment (Marco)
